t: You're on the Old Bailey, a street in the City of London. In the Restoration period, a man named William Atkins lived here. He was an English quack, which is to say a seller of supposed cures. He gained some fame and wealth for his claimed cure for gout. His only published work, from 1694, was A Discourse Shewing the Nature of the Gout. So before this street meant anything else to you, it was the address of a doctor of dubious reputation.
